speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to help me determine the cause, can you describe exactly how the swelling started and if there was any injury involved?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Osteochondroma.

The patient is an 18-month-old with spontaneous right knee swelling and a family history of similar problems, which strongly suggests a genetic bone tumor. Given the age and lack of trauma, an X-ray is the next necessary step to confirm the diagnosis.
